newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: U.S. mulls reducing Peru-Ecuador peace support.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mulls reducing Peru-Ecuador peace support.

text.p: The United States is considering reducing logistical support for international peacekeeping operations on the jungle border between Peru and Ecuador, site of a bloody border clash in February last year, U.S. defence chiefs said Tuesday.

"We do not want it to become a Cyprus operation," U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry told reporters at a meeting of Western hemisphere defence ministers here. He was referring to the U.N. peacekeeping force first established on the divided Mediterranean island in 1964.
The United States, Brazil, Argentina and Chile are guarantors of peace between Peru and Ecuador under the Rio treaty.
In Bariloche, Perry witnessed a handshake for the cameras between Peruvian Defence Minister Gen. Tomas Castillo Meza and his Ecuadorean counterpart Gen. Victor Bayas.
He termed peace operations in the Condor range of the Andes a "tremendous success" and pledged continued support as long as there is progress towards a diplomatic resolution.

The U.S. Commander-in-Chief Southern Command, Lt Gen. Wesley Clark, said Washington would "not necessarily" reduce logistic support for the peacekeeping effort, but added: "It's one of the options being considered."

"We are considering how to transition support in order to encourage the diplomatic resolution of the conflict because we don't want this to become an infinite duration peacekeeping operation," Clark told reporters.
"We want to go beyond preventing the conflict, we want to be able to address the sources of the conflict."
